powerCalc_S116.rule: DD-33 / RP-1 (F-1, CRITICAL) — D33's theory check is made ABLE TO SUCCEED OR FAIL ON THE MERITS, without HARKing. THE A-PRIORI ARGUMENT, pinned BEFORE any recompute (it stands WITHOUT reference to the observed result): a point-tolerance test at 0.02 requires the estimator's sampling SE to be BELOW 0.02. PBO at CSCV split-count S is a mean over C(S, S/2) overlapping combinations; its naive lower-bound SE is sqrt(0.25 / C(S,S/2)). At S=8, C(8,4)=70 -> SE >= sqrt(0.25/70) ~ 0.0598 (and LARGER, because the combinations overlap). THEREFORE the S=8 experiment was NEVER a valid test of a 0.02 tolerance — and this was true before any PBO was computed. At S=16, C(16,8)=12870 -> SE ~ sqrt(0.25/12870) ~ 0.0044, comfortably inside the UNCHANGED, already-pinned 0.02.
powerCalc_S116.route: RAISE THE POWER, KEEP THE TOLERANCE (route a). Power is an A-PRIORI property, computable without any result. Re-running an underpowered experiment at adequate power (S=16) is not tuning — it is running it properly. NO threshold moves, NO SEARCH is incurred. The tolerance stays 0.02.
powerCalc_S116.sIsInsideFrozenSetProof: rigor.pbo(matrix, n_splits: int = 8, ...) takes n_splits as a CALL-SITE PARAMETER (default 8); S=8 was a PIN (cscvAlignment.S in the pins), never frozen code. Raising S to 16 is a change to the HARNESS call (crosscheck.py, NOT in the frozen set), not to rigor.py. The frozen sha 58c88843 does not move. Verified in Phase 0 (F-1's mandate).
powerCalc_S116.empiricalSeMandate: RP-1/RP-2 — the EMPIRICAL SE is COMPUTED and SHOWN (not the naive lower bound): the whole PBO computation is run over >=200 independent seeds under a true-Sharpe-0 null, and the sampling SD of PBO is the empirical SE. The z = (observed_mean - 0.5)/SE is REPORTED as a NUMBER (the distance), never merely a boolean in/out (RP-2). The mean over the null seeds is the powered estimate of PBO; the single-seed S=8 result is not.

The negotiation RANGE (accept several, refuse loudly outside) is the fix regardless of verification — a range that includes the client's version does not refuse it.

adversarialRecord_partA.rule: PART A' — 10 attacks, each with its binding consequence, attacked BEFORE design. findings_closed_substance asserts each consequence holds in the shipped code.
adversarialRecord_partA.A1_changingTheTestIsHARKing: THE SHARPEST ATTACK — 'the instrument was invalid' is exactly the excuse a user would give and you would not accept it. Answered: DD-33's preferred route COSTS NO SEARCH — power is A-PRIORI (SE at S=8 is ~0.06 > 0.02 regardless of the observed PBO), so raising S to 16 is running the experiment PROPERLY, not tuning. The tolerance 0.02 does NOT move. IF the test TYPE had to change (point -> distributional) that WOULD be a search, disclosed as D56 and counted — it does not, so it isn't. The failed 0.02-at-S=8 result STAYS in the record forever. You do not get to delete the test you failed.
adversarialRecord_partA.A2_reTieringAShippedFact: TRUE — a wrong tier left the building through the Socket to downstream models. Corrected loudly (D57); exposure stated: reachableHumans 1, published false, blast radius ZERO — a darkly funny vindication of the reach analysis, said out loud. S117 makes the class unrepeatable: every FACT wall carries a POSITIVE provenance assertion.
adversarialRecord_partA.A3_oracleStalenessAddsATrustedThirdParty: VALID, a real new surface — so it is OWED to V39, not smuggled. IF it ships, the RPC read is a CAPTURE graded like every capture (content-hashed, tiered, UNJUDGEABLE without it), its provider named with exposure disclosed (D60), a public/self-hostable endpoint preferred, mass path staying at TWO dependencies. RP-4: it ships only for a pinned subset with a disclosed coverage fraction, never as a decoration.
adversarialRecord_partA.A4_algebraMovesALineageId: FATAL if it happens — the exit criterion is inside the content hash. S125: ADDITIVE OR IT DOES NOT SHIP; the wall is TWO-SIDED (every fixture lineage id before===after AND every exit evaluation byte-identical, RP-5). OWED to V39; V33 proved the shape (act was addable because it was OUTSIDE the hashed payload; the exit criterion is INSIDE it, so the algebra changes the internal representation and not one byte of the wire format — or it does not ship).
adversarialRecord_partA.A5_eightPhasesShipFourDropResidues: THE REALISTIC FAILURE MODE, and V37 is the evidence. Answered by the SHED ORDER, pinned and enforced: Phases 1,2,3 NEVER shed. This sprint ships 1-3 + 4 and OWES 5/6/7 to V39 — DISCLOSED, not dropped. A sprint that ships only 1-3 is a SUCCESSFUL sprint because it makes what already shipped TRUE.
adversarialRecord_partA.A6_corpusOwedTwiceDroppedTwice: LANDS. Phase 3, NEVER SHEDS. And the honest terminal clause: if the guard catches nothing for a FIFTH consecutive sprint, its efficacy is UNJUDGEABLE, the CORPUS is the weak wall — not the guard — and the gate MUST say so (RP-7).
adversarialRecord_partA.A7_wallBanningNumbersBeatenBySpellingOut: VALID. S126's rule is stated POSITIVELY — prose may NAME a producer, may never RESTATE a value; the wall greps digit-runs AND the rule covers spelled-out numbers. Not a new law — X-DERIVE(b) already says every claim needs a producer, and a number in prose is a claim.
adversarialRecord_partA.A8_firingTriggerThenSheddingAlgebra: would be ignoring my own criterion IF hidden. The trigger did NOT fire this sprint (the set stays at 5 — the two kinds are owed). IF a future sprint reaches 7, the firing is recorded as a FACT with its hash (DD-40, X-CADENCE applied to ourselves). A tool that renders its own fired exits as facts does not get an exception for itself.
adversarialRecord_partA.A9_socketPinMightBeFine: POSSIBLE — and that is exactly the point: nobody checked. X-HONEST: an unverified pin is UNVERIFIED, not 'probably fine.' DD-36: check it, then NEGOTIATE a range rather than pin a point; if the current revision cannot be determined the handshake says UNVERIFIED and it goes to the gate.
adversarialRecord_partA.A10_twoSprintsNoLawConstitutionDead: DONE, not dead — and the evidence is this sprint's own thesis. Every V37 defect was an EXISTING law under-applied (X-REACH(a) the tolerance, X-MOAT the tier, X-HONEST the pin, X-DERIVE(b) the prose). A constitution that already contains the answer to every new defect is complete. The work from here is application, not legislation.

postImplementationRePins_partF.rule: PART F — blocking re-pins for Phase 0. findings_closed_substance asserts each holds in the shipped code.
postImplementationRePins_partF.RP1_powerArgumentAPriori: CRITICAL (F-1) — raising S to 16 is not free unless the power argument stands A-PRIORI. The argument: a point-tolerance test at 0.02 requires SE < 0.02; at S=8 SE ~0.06; therefore S=8 was NEVER a valid test of a 0.02 tolerance — true before any number. It holds a priori (SE is a function of S,N,T), so raising S is a CORRECTION and no search is incurred. And S is NOT inside the frozen set (rigor.pbo takes n_splits as a call param; crosscheck.py is the editable harness) — verified in Phase 0.
postImplementationRePins_partF.RP2_confidenceLevelAPrioriAndZ: HIGH (F-2) — the distributional test (route b) has a free parameter (why 95%?). Fix: the confidence level is pinned with an a-priori justification (the conventional two-sided 0.05, before the gap is known) AND the observed value is reported with its z-score, not merely in/out. Report z=(observed-0.5)/SE and let the pen see the number. (Moot this sprint — route (a) is taken and no distributional test with a confidence level is used to gate; the z is reported regardless.)
postImplementationRePins_partF.RP3_fallbackStatedBeforeAudit: HIGH (F-3) — re-tiering the false-fire count may DESTROY it (UNJUDGEABLE forever if the chart is the only history). Fix: the fallback is stated BEFORE the audit — count over ORGANON's OWN captures (REAL-star, PIT), state the window (short today, grows with the cadence), optionally the retrospective series too tiered RETROSPECTIVE, both shown. It turns the false-fire count into a reason to run the cadence — which is what IN2 asked for.
postImplementationRePins_partF.RP4_oracleCoveragePinnedBeforeBuild: MEDIUM-HIGH (F-4) — oracle-staleness is a fact about a contract ORGANON may not identify (a pool id is not an oracle address; resolution is per-protocol, brittle). Fix: scope it honestly — a named pinned subset, UNJUDGEABLE for the rest, coverage fraction pinned BEFORE building; a 6th kind UNJUDGEABLE for 95% of the shelf is a decoration and does not ship. (OWED to V39 with this constraint attached.)
postImplementationRePins_partF.RP5_algebraWallTwoSided: MEDIUM (F-5) — byte-identity proves serialization, not semantics; a lineage id could be unchanged and the verdict move. Fix: the wall is two-sided — (i) every fixture lineage id unchanged AND (ii) every fixture cycle's exit evaluation byte-identical, including UNJUDGEABLE cases. (OWED to V39 with this constraint attached.)
postImplementationRePins_partF.RP6_doorOrderingMechanical: MEDIUM (F-6) — with many kinds, ORDER becomes a recommendation. Fix: pin the ordering rule (the EXIT_KINDS enum order), asserted by a wall; a 'recommended first'/'most common' ordering is a Halt. Pinned now so V39 inherits it.
postImplementationRePins_partF.RP7_corpusTerminalClauseOnProvenance: MEDIUM (F-7) — an agent that writes its own baits will write baits its guard catches (one catch, clause avoided). Fix: the terminal clause fires on the PROVENANCE of the catch — a catch counts only if the bait came from a different author AND its angle was not enumerated in the pins; else guardEfficacy:UNJUDGEABLE is computed and printed whatever the count says.

delegatedDecisions.rule: Claude Code decides, documents, proceeds. A codebase-answerable question routed back to the Operator is a STALL.
delegatedDecisions.DD33_fixATestThatCannotSucceed: How to fix a test that cannot succeed WITHOUT HARKing? Route (a): RAISE THE POWER, KEEP THE TOLERANCE. Power is a-priori; S=16 -> SE~0.004 < the unchanged 0.02. S is a call param (n_splits), not frozen, so raising it edits the harness (crosscheck.py) not rigor.py. Compute the empirical SE and SHOW it; report z; preserve the S=8 result forever; if 0.6 survives adequate power D33 stays closed (a real finding). NO SEARCH incurred (D56 does not fire).
delegatedDecisions.DD34_isTheChartSeriesPIT: Is the DefiLlama chart series point-in-time honest? No — it is RETROSPECTIVE (the provider's present opinion about the past, revisable). The tier must match the truth: re-tier it RETROSPECTIVE, and count over ORGANON's OWN captures (REAL-star, PIT) where they reach; state the window and what a short window costs the count's authority (UNJUDGEABLE below the floor). State the fact shipped with a wrong tier for one sprint (blast radius zero).
delegatedDecisions.DD35_strangerCanGetIt: What predicate means 'a STRANGER can get this'? The narrowest one a private/authenticated remote cannot satisfy: an unauthenticated credential-free public forge URL AND a committed release-manifest artifact with its SHA-256 (an unauthenticated fetch target). A URL with embedded credentials derives false. Prove it: a seeded authenticated remote derives false.
delegatedDecisions.DD36_currentMcpProtocol: What MCP protocol version do real clients negotiate TODAY? Do not guess — NEGOTIATE a declared range (2024-11-05, 2025-03-26, 2025-06-18 recalled); on an unsupported version refuse loudly naming the range; if the current revision cannot be verified the handshake says UNVERIFIED and it is a gate item. The negotiation range is the fix regardless of verification status.
delegatedDecisions.DD37_canOracleStalenessBeCaptured: Can oracle-staleness be captured? Observable: now - feed.updatedAt and 'feed is a constant' — deterministic reads over the governance screen's existing RPC. UNJUDGEABLE without the read. RP-4: scope the coverage honestly (a pinned subset), pin the fraction before building, no decoration. OWED to V39.
delegatedDecisions.DD38_isUtilizationAlreadyHeld: Is utilization-ceiling derivable from data already held? Lending-pool utilization is standard in the lending senses ORGANON captures (oracle-proven PIT) — free if present, costed if not. OWED to V39 (the check runs there).
delegatedDecisions.DD39_algebraWithoutMovingALineageId: Can the algebra ship WITHOUT moving a single lineage id? ADDITIVE OR IT DOES NOT SHIP: every existing kind serializes byte-identically; the wall is every fixture lineage id before===after AND every exit evaluation byte-identical (RP-5). If byte-identity cannot be proven it does not ship. OWED to V39.
delegatedDecisions.DD40_exitSetTriggerFires: The exit set reaches SEVEN, the trigger FIRES — what now? ORGANON applies X-CADENCE to itself: a fired trigger is a FACT, never an instruction; the build log records the firing with its hash; whether the algebra ships is a matter of the shed order, not the trigger. THIS SPRINT: the set stays at 5, the trigger did NOT fire, recorded as the honest state (owed to V39).
